chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Mufaddal, from Sa'd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, hearts are four: a heart in which is hypocrisy and faith, an inverted heart, an imprinted heart, and a shining, pure heart. So I said, 'What is the shining one?' He said, 'It is like the form of a lamp.' As for the imprinted one, it is the heart of the hypocrite; and as for the shining one, it is the heart of the believer: if He gives, he is grateful, and if He tests him, he is patient; and as for the inverted one, it is the heart of the polytheist.
Then he recited this verse: 'So is one who walks prone on his face better guided or one who walks upright on a straight path?'

As for the heart in which is faith and hypocrisy, they were a people who were in Al-Ta'if. So if death overtook one of them upon his hypocrisy, he perished, and if it overtook him upon his faith, he attained salvation.
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of hearts described in Shia hadith and how do they differ?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates four spiritual states of the heart, distinguishing the radiant, unblemished heart of the true believer from the inverted heart of the polytheist and the sealed heart of the hypocrite. This classification underscores the internal reality of faith, where the believer's heart shines like a lamp, responding to trials with patience and blessings with gratitude. The narration connects these states to the Quranic imagery of upright versus prone walking, highlighting the spiritual trajectory of each type.
